name: Dell XPS 13 9350
description: A compact aluminium ultrabook with a sharp 13.4 inch screen. It fits in any backpack and lasts a full day of lectures, so it suits students who move between buildings all day.

name: MacBook Air 13 M3
description: A silent, fanless laptop with very long battery life. It handles notes, coding and light photo editing, and it stays cool on your lap in a crowded library.

name: MacBook Air 15 M3
description: The bigger Air gives you a 15.3 inch screen for split-screen research without adding much weight. Good for students who read long papers and want room for two windows.

name: Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x
description: An ARM-based ultrabook with one of the longest battery lives in this list. The bright OLED screen is easy on the eyes for long study sessions.

name: ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED
description: A light 14 inch laptop with an OLED panel at a fair price. A strong all-rounder for first-year students who want quality without a premium price.

name: ASUS ROG Strix G16
description: A powerful gaming laptop with a fast 165 Hz screen and a strong graphics card. It also handles 3D modelling and machine learning labs, but it needs its charger nearby.

name: Lenovo Legion 5i Gen 9
description: A well-cooled gaming machine with 32 GB of RAM. It is a safe pick for engineering students who run heavy simulations and also want to play after class.

name: MSI Katana 15
description: An entry gaming laptop with a dedicated graphics card at a mid-range price. Expect short battery life, so it works best as a desk machine.

name: HP Victus 15
description: A budget-friendly gaming laptop with a calm design that does not look out of place in class. Good value for students who game a little and code a lot.

name: Acer Nitro V 15
description: The cheapest way into PC gaming in this list. The 8 GB of RAM can be upgraded later, which makes it a smart long-term buy.

name: HP Spectre x360 14
description: A premium convertible that flips into a tablet for handwritten notes. It comes with a pen, so it suits students who sketch diagrams and annotate slides.

name: Lenovo Yoga 7i 2-in-1
description: A flexible 2-in-1 with a 360 degree hinge and a comfortable keyboard. Use it as a laptop in class and as a tablet for reading at home.

name: Microsoft Surface Pro 11
description: The lightest device here: a tablet with a detachable keyboard. Perfect for note taking with a pen, but the keyboard cover is sold separately.

name: ASUS Vivobook S 14 Flip
description: An affordable convertible with a touch screen and pen support. A friendly first laptop for students who want tablet mode on a small budget.

name: Dell Inspiron 14 2-in-1
description: A sturdy 2-in-1 with 16 GB of RAM at a mid price. It handles many browser tabs and video calls while switching to tablet mode for reading.

name: MacBook Pro 14 M4 Pro
description: A creator laptop with a colour-accurate screen and huge battery life. Built for video editing, music production and big code projects.

name: ASUS ProArt P16
description: A large 4K OLED creator laptop with a dial for creative apps. Made for design and architecture students who need screen space and power.

name: Dell XPS 16 9640
description: A big-screen creator laptop with a clean, minimal design. Strong for photo editing, CAD work and multitasking across many apps.

name: MSI Prestige 16 AI Evo
description: A light 16 inch creator laptop with 32 GB of RAM and long battery life. A balanced choice for students who edit media on the move.

name: Acer Aspire 3
description: A simple and affordable laptop for notes, online classes and office work. A good backup machine or a first laptop on a tight budget.

name: Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3
description: A slim budget laptop with a full-size keyboard and number pad. Great for spreadsheets, reports and everyday university tasks.

name: HP 15 fd0
description: A reliable everyday laptop with a modern Core i5 processor. It runs programming tools and many browser tabs without slowing down.

name: ASUS Vivobook Go 15
description: The lowest price in the list. Enough for reading, writing and video lectures, and the hinge opens flat for sharing your screen with a study group.

name: Dell Inspiron 15 3530
description: A budget laptop with 16 GB of RAM, which is rare at this price. It stays smooth with many apps open, so it suits computer science students.
